assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology defined the incretin effect on glucose-dependent insulin secretion and led to therapies that now transform treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with cardiovascular and renal benefit. Originality, clarity and breadth of clinical impact are exceptional, and the physiology-to-medicine arc fits the prize well.
assessment.attribution: Holst (incretin physiology, GLP-1 biology), Drucker (proglucagon-derived peptide biology and GLP-2, therapeutic translation) and Mojsov (identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) form) are the best-supported basic-science trio from the supplied names. Lotte Bjerre Knudsen is the key industrial translator of liraglutide/semaglutide, but I judge the basic discoveries to be the more prize-appropriate core. Other contributors, such as Habener, are not in the supplied credit and I cannot add them.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is confirmed by decades of independent work and large outcome trials, and the interpretation is stable. Recognition is timely and arguably pressing given clinical scale.
uncertainties: Credit allocation among Mojsov, Habener-group contributors and others is disputed and I have not verified the details.
Whether translational (Knudsen) or basic contributions should be preferred is a committee judgment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of TNF as a dominant driver in rheumatoid arthritis synovium and its clinical blockade established the cytokine-targeted paradigm for chronic inflammatory disease, with anti-TNF now used across RA, IBD, psoriasis and spondyloarthritis. The impact on patient outcomes is large and the logic from mechanism to therapy is clear.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini led the translational chain from synovial cytokine biology to the first clinical trials of anti-TNF, and the supplied credit is a clean two-person configuration. Fits a fair prize without needing the industry antibody developers; those who made the antibodies or the TNF cloning are outside the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of clinical use and independent confirmation; the finding is mature, and recognition is arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Relative weighting of the earlier TNF biology (cloning, TNF biology in other settings) versus clinical translation is uncertain.
Not independently verified by me beyond existing knowledge.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells with chimeric antigen receptors produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and opened a new therapeutic class (living drugs). Originality, clinical effect and the impetus for further cell-therapy research are high.
assessment.attribution: June (clinical CD19 CAR-T with costimulation), Sadelain (CD28 costimulatory design and CAR engineering) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell therapy and early engineered-T-cell trials) are plausible from the supplied names. The credit is not clean: Zelig Eshhar's original CAR concept is not among the supplied names, and this weakens the configuration.
assessment.maturity: Approved products and multi-year follow-up exist, but long-term durability, toxicity and limited solid-tumor efficacy leave the story still evolving.
uncertainties: Missing foundational contributor (Eshhar) in the supplied credit.
Whether the field is mature enough or best waited on.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway explains how cytosolic DNA triggers type I interferon and inflammation, linking innate sensing to infection, autoimmunity (e.g., interferonopathies, lupus), cancer immunity and senescence. A clear mechanistic discovery with wide conceptual reach, of direct relevance to autoimmune pathogenesis.
assessment.attribution: Chen discovered cGAS and the cyclic dinucleotide second messenger cGAMP; Barber identified STING. This is the most defensible two-person core from the supplied names. Others (Ishikawa, Wu, Sun) made contributions to STING/cGAS discovery but I consider them secondary.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is confirmed independently with structures and genetics; therapeutic translation (STING agonists/inhibitors) is not yet delivered, so recognition could be seen as somewhat early, but the basic discovery is solid.
uncertainties: Clinical benefit is not yet established.
Credit boundaries between STING identification groups are uncertain to me.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery and cloning of IL-6 and its receptor, and the therapeutic blockade with tocilizumab, established a second major cytokine-targeted anti-inflammatory strategy for RA, giant cell arteritis, cytokine release syndrome and other diseases. Strong bench-to-bedside link.
assessment.attribution: Kishimoto and Hirano are a natural two-person pairing for the discovery and cloning of IL-6 and its receptor/signaling. The supplied names fit without trouble.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with decades of clinical use and independent confirmation. Its cytokine-blockade concept partly overlaps with TNF, which could reduce incremental novelty if TNF is recognized.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would recognise both TNF and IL-6 in nearby years.
Original IL-6 discovery history involved parallel groups whose credit I cannot verify.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Splice-modulating antisense therapy for SMA (nusinersen) turned a lethal infant disease into a treatable one and validated an RNA-targeted therapeutic principle. The mechanistic discovery of SMN2 exon 7 splicing control and its translation are well-defined.
assessment.attribution: Krainer (splicing mechanism and ASO design for SMN2) and Bennett (ASO chemistry/platform and development) form a coherent pair from the supplied names. Others, notably Adrian Krainer's collaborators and the SMN gene discoverers (Melki, Lefebvre), are outside this credit.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with clear clinical benefit and broader ASO uses emerging, so the principle is confirmed. Timing is reasonable but the field is still developing.
uncertainties: Weighing of gene discovery versus therapeutic development.
Industrial role of Ionis/Biogen raises usual attribution questions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics created a general method for causal control of defined cell populations, transforming neural circuit research and being applied toward vision restoration. The methodological and conceptual impact on physiology is very large.
assessment.attribution: Hegemann and Nagel (with Bamberg) discovered and characterised channelrhodopsins; Deisseroth and Boyden demonstrated neuronal control and extended the toolkit; Miesenböck made an early related approach. Six credited people exceed the three-person limit, so any prize configuration leaves out deserving contributors. My selection is a judgment call.
assessment.maturity: Widely confirmed and used, with early clinical translation; the technique is mature, though therapeutic payoff is limited so far.
uncertainties: Severe credit allocation difficulty among six candidates.
Prize emphasis on discovery versus tool development.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCR-ABL kinase inhibition with imatinib converted chronic myeloid leukemia into a manageable condition and established the model of molecularly targeted cancer therapy, with resistance-mechanism work (dasatinib and others) extending it. Very high clinical impact.
assessment.attribution: Druker (clinical development), Lydon (compound discovery and kinase inhibitor program) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors) form a plausible trio. Janet Rowley, Nowell/Hungerford and Nicholas Lydon's chemists add attribution complexity, and prior recognition (Lasker 2009) occurred for part of this.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with long-term survival data. The story is complete, but an older discovery.
uncertainties: Possible overlap of credit with earlier chromosomal/oncogene discoveries.
Whether Lydon's contribution is separable from the company team.
